title: Hip examination
stem: Cubicle 22. Mr Ho, 64, has had increasing right groin pain for 6 months, worse walking, and now struggles to put on his socks. Examine his hip and explain your findings.

phases.title: Examine
phases.goal: Walk and stand; look and measure; feel; move; the Thomas test; then the knee and the foot.

notes:
Checked against NICE NG226 (Osteoarthritis, 2022) and standard hip examination.

Look (gait: antalgic or Trendelenburg; standing: Trendelenburg test for abductor weakness; scars, wasting, pelvic tilt, leg length — true (ASIS to medial malleolus) versus apparent (umbilicus to medial malleolus)), feel (greater trochanter tenderness for bursitis), move (flexion, extension, abduction, adduction, internal and external rotation — internal rotation is lost first in OA), special tests (Thomas test for fixed flexion deformity; FADIR/FABER). Examine the lumbar spine and the knee (referred pain), and neurovascular status.

OA is a clinical diagnosis in people 45 or over with activity-related joint pain and morning stiffness of 30 minutes or less (NICE); X-ray is not needed to diagnose it, but in the ED it helps exclude fracture or other pathology. Management: exercise, weight loss, analgesia, walking aids, and orthopaedic referral when symptoms affect quality of life despite treatment. Your notes list look (Trendelenburg, gait, leg length, Galeazzi), feel, move and Thomas test — matching.

The examination is a focused 3D examination, checked step by step against Geeky Medics (hip examination: gait; Trendelenburg test, fingers on the iliac crests, the pelvis dropping on the lifted side meaning weak abductors of the standing hip; true leg length ASIS to medial malleolus, apparent umbilicus to medial malleolus; trochanter palpation; passive flexion (normal 120°), internal rotation with hip and knee at 90° by moving the foot laterally (40°), external by moving it medially (45°), abduction (45°) and adduction (30°) with a hand on the contralateral iliac crest; Thomas test with a hand under the lumbar spine and the other hip fully flexed; complete with the knee, lumbar spine and neurovascular status) and Arthritis UK's examination of the hip (internal rotation the first movement affected in hip disease; groin tenderness for true hip problems). Mr Ho's osteoarthritic right hip: flexion 95°, internal rotation 5°, external 20°, abduction 20°, adduction 15°, a 15° fixed flexion deformity.

Perfect script checked against NICE NG226 and standard hip examination, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme.

body.intro: Mr Ho is lying on the couch in shorts, both legs bare. Examine his right hip: choose below, or tap the hip.

findings.warmth@hip-L: The left hip: normal temperature, the same.
findings.press-at@hip-R: Greater trochanter: not tender. Not trochanteric bursitis.
findings.press-at@groin-R: The groin, over the joint: tender; he winces.
findings.move-knee@knee-R: The right knee bends and straightens fully, without pain.
findings.touch@foot-R: Feels light touch normally over the foot.

steps.label: Examine the hip
steps.hint: Walk and the Trendelenburg test; inspect and measure; feel; flexion, rotation at 90°, abduction and adduction; the Thomas test; then the knee, pulses and sensation.

Look.r: An antalgic gait: he spends as little time as he can on the right leg.

Look.t: Trendelenburg test: stand on each leg, my fingers on your iliac crests
Look.r: Standing on the right leg, his pelvis drops on the left: positive on the right (weak right hip abductors). On the left leg it stays level.

Look.t: Inspect both hips and legs on the couch
Look.r: No scars or swelling. The right thigh is a little wasted, and the right leg lies slightly bent at the hip.
Look.mark: Inspects for scars, wasting and deformity

Look.r: True lengths equal (ASIS to medial malleolus). Apparent: the right 2 cm shorter (umbilicus to medial malleolus), from the pelvic tilt of a fixed flexion.
Look.mark: Measures true and apparent leg length

Feel.t: Feel the temperature over both hips
Feel.r: Normal and equal: no sign of a hot, septic joint.

Feel.t: Press on the greater trochanter and in the groin
Feel.r: Tender in the groin, over the joint; the trochanter is not tender.

Move.r: Flexion stops at 95°, painful at the end (normal about 120°).

Move.t: Internal and external rotation with the hip and knee at 90°
Move.r: Internal rotation 5° and painful; external rotation 20°. Internal rotation is lost first in osteoarthritis.
Move.mark: Tests rotations; finds loss of internal rotation

Move.t: Abduction and adduction, the pelvis steadied
Move.mark: Tests abduction and adduction with the pelvis stabilised

Special.r: As his left hip comes up to his chest, the right thigh lifts off the couch: a 15° fixed flexion deformity.

Complete.t: The knee, the foot pulses and sensation
Complete.r: The knee moves fully and painlessly; foot pulses present; sensation normal.
Complete.mark: Examines the joint below and neurovascular status
Complete.do: move knee-R & feel dp-R & cotton foot-R

steps.ask: Thank you. Please present your findings.
steps.label: Present
steps.hint: Likely right hip OA; X-ray; conservative care; referral.

opts.t: Right hip osteoarthritis: groin pain, an antalgic gait, a positive Trendelenburg, apparent shortening, loss of internal rotation first, and a 15° fixed flexion deformity on the Thomas test. I would complete with the lumbar spine.
opts.mark: Presents findings and diagnosis; completes with the lumbar spine

opts.t: A pelvis and hip X-ray to exclude other causes; analgesia, exercise, weight loss, a walking stick in the left hand, and orthopaedic referral.
opts.mark: Management plan including stick in the opposite hand

qs.a: Fixed flexion deformity of the hip
wrong: A true leg length discrepancy from the ASIS
A knee effusion on the patellar tap test

qs.q: Positive Trendelenburg on the right means…
qs.a: Pelvis drops on the left when standing on the right
wrong: The right knee buckles when standing on it
Pain in the right groin on weight-bearing
The left leg is short when measured from ASIS

qs.q: First movement lost in hip OA?
True leg length is measured from…

qs.a: Loss of joint space, osteophytes, sclerosis, cysts
wrong: Periosteal reaction and a sunburst pattern
Soap-bubble lucency in the femoral head
Periarticular erosions with osteopenia and joint-space loss

badge.name: Hip Check
badge.flavor: Internal rotation goes first. Stick in the other hand.

cards.q: Apparent leg length is measured from…
options: Greater trochanter to the lateral knee joint line
Hamstrings on the same side as the hip
Hip adductors on the opposite side
cards.why: Pelvis drops on the opposite side.

cards.q: NICE: OA can be diagnosed clinically in people aged…
options: Any age, but only once an X-ray confirms it

cards.q: Walking stick for right hip pain goes in…
cards.why: Reduces load on the painful hip.

options: Infants for developmental dysplasia of the hip
cards.why: Knee heights compared with hips flexed.

script.say: Watch him walk. Trendelenburg test: stand on each leg. Inspect both hips. True and apparent leg lengths.
script.do: Antalgic gait on the right. Standing on the right, the pelvis drops on the left: positive on the right. Right thigh wasted, the leg slightly bent. True lengths equal; apparent shortening on the right from pelvic tilt.

script.say: Feel the temperature over both hips. Press on the greater trochanter and in the groin.
script.do: Normal temperature. Groin tender; trochanter not tender.

script.say: Passive flexion; internal and external rotations with the hip and knee at 90°; abduction and adduction, the pelvis steadied. Thomas test.
script.do: Flexion 95°, internal rotation 5° and painful, external rotation 20°, abduction 20°, adduction 15°. The right thigh lifts off the couch: 15° fixed flexion deformity.

script.say: The knee, the foot pulses and sensation.

Right hip osteoarthritis: groin pain, an antalgic gait, a positive Trendelenburg, apparent shortening, loss of internal rotation first, and a 15° fixed flexion deformity on the Thomas test. I would complete with the lumbar spine. A pelvis and hip X-ray to exclude other causes; analgesia, exercise, weight loss, a walking stick in the left hand, and orthopaedic referral.
